item.title: 2: Daily Halacha: Torah on Moadim
item.description:
Why are the festivals called Moadim, and how should the day be divided? The word means a meeting set by Israel through the calendar. The Gemara's dispute between Rabbi Yehoshua and Rabbi Eliezer is decided as half the day for God and half for ourselves, with prayer and Torah counting toward God's half.

item.title: 4: Daily Halacha: Rejoicing & שמחה on the Hag Part 1
item.description:
How do you fulfil the misvah of simhah on the festivals? Unlike Shabbat, the festivals carry a command to rejoice, and Rabbi Yehudah ben Betera in the Gemara says each person rejoices in what suits them: men, women and children. The Rabbi covers meat and wine and why a purely dairy meal on Shavuot is not the original custom.

item.title: 6: Daily Halacha: Hadlakat Nerot on Yom Tov
item.description:

item.title: 7: Daily Halacha: Introduction to Melakhah on Yom Tov
item.description:
How is Yom Tov different from Shabbat in terms of melakhah? Yom Tov has greater simhah, but Shabbat has greater kedushah. Okhel nefesh makes food-related work permitted in all cases, though not every melakhah is permitted, and any permitted act must benefit Yom Tov itself.

item.title: 8: Daily Halacha: Melakhot on Yom Tov for a Non-Jew or Convert
item.description:
May a Jew invite a non-Jew, or someone in the process of conversion, to a Yom Tov meal? Cooking for non-Jews is barred, so inviting is prohibited though a guest who arrives uninvited may eat. Rav Shlomo Zalman Auerbach permits a serious convert, but no extra cooking.

item.title: 9: Daily Halacha: Preparing Food on Yom Tov: Could It Have Been Done Before?
item.description:
How far does the heter of okhel nefesh stretch on Yom Tov? Food one simply fancies may be cooked even with other food available, and most food is better fresh, but food that gains nothing from being cooked on Yom Tov should be prepared beforehand. The heter does not cover utensils.

item.title: 11: Daily Halacha: Extinguishing a Flame on Yom Tov
item.description:
May one put out a flame or lower the gas on Yom Tov? Extinguishing, including weakening the flame, is forbidden, but for the needs of food, such as stopping fruit from burning, one may lower it. Doing so indirectly, by letting boiling water overflow, is permitted. Lighting from an existing flame was covered the day before.

item.title: 12: Daily Halacha: Manipulating Timers on Yom Tov
item.description:

item.title: 17: Daily Halacha: Eruv Tavshilin Part 1: Reasons and Origins
item.description:
With Yom Tov running into Shabbat three times this year, why is an Eruv Tavshilin needed? The Shulhan Arukh rules that a cooked and a baked dish are both set aside, though a cooked dish alone is enough after the fact.
